documents.title: Faculty Resources for Artificial Intelligence (AI) / Generative AI
documents.summary: A faculty resource page from the Learning and Educational Center that advises instructors to write a syllabus AI policy, explain it to students and discuss it often. It warns against detectors, recommends restructuring courses, and covers privacy, ethics, access and career readiness. It sets no binding rule for students and points to a separate university AI policy.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no stance on student AI use; it says "Effectively integrating Generative AI requires both proactive conversations with students and a clear syllabus policy" and leaves the content of the policy to each instructor, so it delegates.

units.why: The Learning and Educational Center states the page 'serves to familiarize, support, and guide Nova Southeastern University faculty in AI matters', an office stating its commitment to support faculty learning about AI. It is a statement of purpose by an office (actor admin, informs), type P63 because it is faculty support rather than a university-wide framework.

The office is the actor; it is a statement of purpose, so informs.

documents.unit: Office of the Provost / Student Handbook (academic standards)
documents.title: Student Handbook 2025-2026: Academic Standards (generative AI clause)
documents.summary: The handbook's academic standards section bans students' use of generative AI on coursework and assessments without prior faculty permission. Only this sentence in the handbook addresses AI; it sits within the original-work standard.
documents.stance_why: AI is "expressly prohibited" on coursework "without the prior permission of their faculty member", so it is banned unless permitted, which is restrict.

units.why: The handbook defines the scope of the AI rule: 'generative artificial intelligence (e.g., ChatGPT, Google Bard, DALL-E, Midjourney, etc.) or similar resources'. It is a definition of what AI is covered, P61, informs.
units.anchor: generative artificial intelligence (e.g., ChatGPT, Google Bard, DALL -E, Midjourney, etc.)
units.frag_start: Students’ use of generative artificial intelligence
units.resolution_why: Only coder A found this unit. The parenthetical 'generative artificial intelligence (e.g., ChatGPT, Google Bard, DALL-E, Midjourney, etc.) or similar resources' defines what the ban covers, a real scope statement, so kept as P61 informs.

units.why: The handbook says students' AI use 'on any coursework or academic assessments without the prior permission of their faculty member ... is expressly prohibited': banned unless the faculty member permits, which is the default rule (P06); student, during-work, must-not.

units.fit_note: Applies to all coursework and assessments university-wide, not only when a syllabus is silent. / Ban is on all coursework and assessments, with permission resting with the individual faculty member.
units.resolution_why: Coders split on phase (A general, B during-work). The ban applies to 'any coursework or academic assessments', i.e. the student's work, so during-work. P06, must-not, restrict are agreed.

units.why: The handbook bans AI use 'in any way that violates the academic standards of NSU and/or a student's academic program', placing it under the academic standards, i.e. misconduct (P36); no detection or sanction is stated, so phase is during-work.

notes: Only the Academic Standards original-work clause in the handbook mentions generative AI. The LEC page links to NSU's AI website with the university AI policy, which was not in the collected text and was not coded. Doc 1 is guidance for faculty; many units are advice addressed to instructors. Reconciled: A-only units dropped as not AI policy statements: the 'NSU's AI website to read about the University's AI policy' pointer (A: P56, fit_note 'Only points to a separate policy; its content is not stated here.'; navigation, and the policy page itself was not collected), 'Last updated February 2025' (A: P54, fit_note 'Only a date stamp, not a statement that the policy will be revisited.'; metadata), and two handbook original-work sentences ('must be the original work of the student', P29, fit_note 'General original-work rule, not specific to AI.'; 'Exams and tests are original work when no unauthorized aid', P22, fit_note 'Bans unauthorized aid generally; AI is not named in this sentence.'), because neither mentions AI. Coder B's note: many instructor-facing advice units use unit_stance neutral because they recommend practices rather than take a position on student AI use; the reconciliation adopts that for matched units.
